title: Clarify rate semantics, Retry-After handling, and idempotency for streaming/tool-calls in OpenAI adapter
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers and SDKs expect OpenAI-compat semantics for rate limits, Retry-After handling, and idempotency keys, but our adapter had subtle mismatches for streaming and tool/function-calling workflows which caused inconsistent retry behavior and duplicate tool invocations. This PR standardizes: 1) rate limit error mapping and payloads to match OpenAI conventions, including 'retry_after_seconds' and a consistent top-level 'type' of 'rate_limit' in the error object; 2) Retry-After header parsing that accepts both seconds and HTTP-date formats and surfaces a normalized numeric retry_after_seconds in both headers and JSON body; 3) idempotency semantics for streaming and function/tool-calling endpoints: the server will record idempotency keys for in-flight and completed invocations, return 409 + structured error when a duplicate non-idempotent request is detected, and permit safe reconnect/resume semantics for streaming where possible; 4) explicit guidance in the OpenAI adapter for SDKs on safe retry/backoff strategies and when to re-use idempotency keys for partial/complete responses. Changes include behavior and schema compatibility shims in the OpenAI adapter, runtime changes to the streaming multiplexer to persist partial KV checkpoints keyed by idempotency, API tests and e2e scenarios that emulate flaky upstream connections, and updated docs/examples. Checklist: - [x] Implement Retry-After parsing and normalized error payloads - [x] Persist idempotency state for streaming/tool calls (in memory for test + DurableStore for prod) - [x] Add unit + integration tests covering duplicate key paths and HTTP-date Retry-After - [x] Update OpenAI adapter docs and SDK notes - [x] Run full e2e and perf smoke tests Summary of impact: Backwards compatible for well-behaved clients. Clients relying on malformed Retry-After or on ambiguous duplicate behavior will now see deterministic errors and a numeric retry_after_seconds field to consume. Internal runtime changes add a small durable write per idempotent invocation; measured cost is minor vs value of avoiding duplicate tool side-effects.
